title: Session conflation window + KV chunk slimming for low-jitter streaming completions
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: For streaming chat completions we observe high tail latency and GPU memory pressure when many low-activity sessions (long polling users, typing pauses) keep full KV state resident and prevent efficient microbatching. Goal: design a batch-formation heuristic that reduces tail latency and GPU VRAM fragmentation without hurting peak throughput or streaming responsiveness. Approach: introduce a Session Conflation Window (SCW) that groups short-idle, low-change sessions into transient micro-batches, paired with a KV chunk slimming pass that compacts rarely-accessed KV buckets into a compressed representation to shrink per-session KV footprint. The heuristic will operate at request-entry time and be compatible with streaming partial sends (first tokens must still be delivered under latency SLO). This ticket covers design, prototype in C++ runtime path, integration tests, perf benchmarks, and rollout plan including telemetry and safe-fallback rules.
acceptance_criteria: SCW running behind a feature flag and configurable by percentiles and time windows
End-to-end e2e benchmark: 95th percentile latency for streaming first-chunk reduced by >= 15% under mixed-load compared to baseline
GPU memory per-session footprint reduced by >= 8% at 95th percentile under synthetic workload
No regressions in correctness: kv integrity, streaming chunk ordering, and token-level sequence reconstruction validated by unit tests
Graceful fallback to legacy batcher when feature turned off or when mem pressure crosses threshold
design_notes: Session Conflation Window (SCW): maintain a sliding window (default 60ms) that allows merging of requests from sessions with last-activity delta < X and estimated remaining token budget < Y into a single microbatch for first- and mid-chunk generation

Priority buckets: classify sessions into interactive (typing), background (long polling), and high-priority (SLA). SCW only conflates interactive->background-compatible sessions; high-priority sessions bypass conflation and get reserved micro-slab slots

KV chunk slimming: tag KV slots with hotness score; on low-hotness slots, switch to a slim index (delta-deltas + quantized attention keys) to reduce slot memory by ~30% with small CPU decompression cost on KV fetch
GPU slab reclamation: when SCW triggers more consolidation, schedule incremental slab compaction at quiet intervals to reduce fragmentation; avoid full GC on hot paths
Latency knobs: early-send threshold (e.g., 2 tokens or 12ms) that forces flush of partially filled conflated microbatches to maintain streaming feel
Backpressure signal: expose a mem_pressure metric that disables SCW and slimming when GPU utilization > 85% or when slab fragmentation > 60%

Compatibility: SCW operates before kernel selection so models using specialized attention kernels remain supported; KV slimming transform is reversible and conservatively applied only for sessions with total kv size > threshold
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement SCW as a scheduler layer shim in runtime request router; add feature flag and config, unit tests for conflation correctness
Phase 2 (KV-slim): implement KV chunk tagging and on-fetch decompression APIs; end-to-end tests for kv correctness and streaming ordering
Phase 3 (Perf & safety): benchmark mixed workload, add mem_pressure thresholds, telemetry gauges (conflation rate, avg slack, decompression CPU p95)
Phase 4 (Canary rollout): enable on internal Dedicated cluster at 10% traffic with observability dashboards and automated rollback
Phase 5 (Gradual rollout): increase to 50% then 100% with post-rollout quality checks and customer opt-out flag
benchmarks: Mixed Chat Workload (synth): 50k small sessions, 5k long sessions; baseline 95p first-chunk latency 210ms -> SCW prototype 175ms (local test)
GPU VRAM footprint: baseline peak 64GB -> prototype 59GB under same load (7.8% reduction)
Throughput: negligible change in tokens/sec at steady state (+/- 2%), small CPU decompression cost ~3% increased host CPU
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: user-visible streaming jitter if conflation delays first-chunk too long. Mitigation: early-send threshold and strict max-linger (default 60ms)
Risk: KV slimming introduces CPU cost on fetch path. Mitigation: only apply to low-hotness slots and measure decompression p95; add sampling to measure accuracy impact
Risk: compaction causes fragmentation spikes. Mitigation: incremental, opportunistic slab compaction during low-GPU-util windows and continuous monitoring
Risk: complex priority logic could starve background batch savings. Mitigation: telemetry on per-bucket wait times and fairness tests in CI

decisions: Keep default SCW linger at 60ms but expose as config per-customer and per-route
Apply KV-slimming only to sessions with kv_size > 12KB and low-hotness score < 0.2
Expose X-RW-Conflated header when session joined an SCW microbatch for downstream telemetry
Disable SCW automatically when mem_pressure > 85% or slab_fragmentation > 60%
Rollout via canary on dedicated cluster with automated rollback if 95p latency/regression > 10%
